text: Kingsmoor FC a pris un super départ avec Viktor Quinlan qui a marqué deux buts en 12 minutes, dont un penalty, donnant l’avantage 2-0 à son équipe [#152] [#222]. Mais Westport Albion a riposté vite grâce à Rafael Delacroix, qui a égalisé avec deux buts avant la mi-temps, à 2-2 [#401] [#553]. Après la pause, Kenji Rahman a donné l'avantage à Westport, mais malgré un carton rouge pour Felix Barros de Kingsmoor à la 81', Luca Iversen a sauvé son équipe en égalisant à la 82e minute, fixant le score à 3-3 [#983] [#1495] [#1516]. Les deux équipes ont beaucoup testé le gardien adverse, avec Kingsmoor jouant large et tentant des centres, tandis que Westport privilégiait un jeu rapide et direct. Quinlan a brillé avec 10 interceptions et 3 tacles, montrant qu'il défendait aussi fort que son équipe attaquait [#222] [#565]. Ce match a eu de belles stratégies et de la tension jusqu’au bout, un vrai régal !

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Viktor Quinlan scored twice early to put Kingsmoor FC 2-0 up by 12' [#152, #222].
- Westport Albion leveled the game with two goals from Rafael Delacroix before halftime, making it 2-2 at 30' [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman gave Westport Albion a 3-2 lead in the 51st minute [#983].
- Felix Barros of Kingsmoor FC received a second yellow card and was sent off at 81' [#1495].
- Luca Iversen scored the equalizer for Kingsmoor FC at 82', finalizing the 3-3 draw [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC’s early lead, including a penalty goal and a well-constructed open-play goal at 12', came from regains that triggered a sequence of 8 passes over 26 seconds involving wide players and the striker Quinlan, who finished with a medium-assist from Duarte. This reflects their 4-4-2 formation with a wide crossing style and structured buildup from turnovers, exploiting flank overloads and crossing opportunities [222][152].

- Westport Albion responded with quick regains leading to goals at 22' and 30' through Delacroix. Their goals arose from rapid, direct vertical passing sequences, including short and cross assists, within 7-10 passes and around 25-40 seconds, highlighting their 4-4-2 formation and direct vertical style aiming for quick penetration and crosses into the box [401][553].

- Both teams created several big chances by combining short and medium passes, showing balanced buildup even for Westport despite their direct style. The high number of interceptions and tackles by Kingsmoor’s Quinlan (10 interceptions, 3 tackles) underlines proactive pressing and ball recovery, consistent with their possession and moderate PPDA values, focusing on wide crossing play after winning the ball high [222][565].

- Tactical changes reflected the match state: Kingsmoor chasing a 2-3 deficit at 65' upped their press intensity and directness, pushing higher line height to regain possession quicker and exploit their crossing strengths; while Westport, after taking the lead, dropped deeper and slowed tempo to protect their advantage with lower press and line height, illustrating the defensive posture supported by their vertical, direct style to absorb pressure and hit on counters [1187][1459].

- The late equalizer for Kingsmoor at 82' came shortly after a red card for their player Barros, from a quick regain and a short cross assist, showing resilience and effective use of their wide crossing style even when down to 10 men. This suggests their wide play and crossing can quickly threaten even under numerical disadvantage [1495][1516].
